Subject: Rapid Fallback SLA requirements and pricing ask

Hi Alex,

Thanks for taking this — Brightline is kicking off procurement for an inference platform to support our new clinical triage product. We have a few specific requirements for premium SLA/retainer coverage before we can move to procurement:

- Guaranteed availability target: 99.99% regional with documented failover to a secondary region
- P1 response: initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes and 15-minute remediation window for critical failures (we understand some remediation may require escalation)
- 24/7 escalation to engineering (we need a named contact or on-call rotation)
- Availability "insurance": a sample schedule showing service credits for 1hr/4hr/24hr outages
- Multi-year pricing options and an incentive for early renewal / multi-year commit

Can you send a pricing/packaging outline and any addendum language you typically include for "fallback insurance" or retainer coverage? We're also interested in how Dedicated capacity vs hosted affects both price and ability to provide deeper guarantees.

I've attached our RFP checklist to this message (Brightline_RFP_SLA_questions.xlsx). Procurement will iterate on contract language but wanted to see your baseline commercials first.

Looking to schedule a short sync next week if possible.

Best,

Samantha Cho
VP, Infrastructure & Cloud
Brightline Health

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. We've put together a concise "Rapid Fallback" bundle that maps to the items you called out; attaching the three-pager and a line-item matrix so procurement can review. High level:

- Rapid-Fallback bundle (hosted): 99.99% regional SLA, automatic cross-region failover policy, 24/7 P1 escalation to on-call + engineering escalation ladder.
- Insurance credits: tiered credit schedule (1hr=5% monthly credit, 4hr=20%, 24hr=60%), with a defined measurement and reporting cadence.
- Response windows: 15-min ack for P1s; target remediation SLA depends on failure class (we'll include runbook examples).
- Dedicated option: Dedicated pools allow more aggressive credits and an elevated availability SLA (99.995%) and deeper RTOs because we can reserve capacity — pricing is higher but we can stretch discounts for committed spend.

Commercials (summary):
- 12-month hosted commitment: baseline price X; 7% standard multi-year discount if you sign 12 months; 12% if you sign 24 months.
- Dedicated (24-month commit): additional 10-15% premium over hosted list, but we can offer an extra 5% off the Dedicated list for a 24-month commit.
- Add-on: 24/7 named on-call + quarterly runbook tabletop exercises available as a retainer (flat monthly fee).

Next steps: 1) Quick call to confirm expected peak token throughput + model footprint (this drives Dedicated sizing). 2) We will produce an updated commercial with redlineable SLA addendum and DocuSign-ready quote.

I've cc'd Laura (Sales Director) for commercial approvals and Jonas (Solutions) to confirm sizing implications. Proposed time: https://cal.com/alexm/brightline-sla-call

Laura/Jonas — forwarding Brightline's initial ask. Key negotiation points to flag:

- They specifically asked for "availability insurance" example schedule and a stronger early-renewal incentive. Procurement hinted at a desire for a 20% discount if we include additional contractual credits.
- They will evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated primarily on whether we can commit to the 15-min P1 ack + named engineering escalation. If we push back on 20% discount, what is our counter?

My suggested approach: offer 12% for 24-month hosted (to meet their multi-year ask), or 15% for 24-month Dedicated with a one-time onboarding fee rolled into TCV. If procurement insists on deeper credits, we should require a higher commit or an SLA carve-out limiting credits against third-party infra incidents.

Jonas — can you confirm the cost delta to guarantee 15-min P1 + runbook tabletop retainer for the hosted case (does it materially increase OPEX)?

Thanks — Alex

Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jonas' inline reply:

> Alex — quick read: 15-min ack is fine (on-call routing), the material cost comes from guaranteeing remediation RTOs and reserving standby capacity. For hosted, we can meet the ack SLA but remediation within 15 mins reliably requires reserved capacity or pre-warmed instances. That pushes us toward Dedicated if they need strong RTOs. For pricing, the 15% off Dedicated for 24-month commitment seems reasonable if we include an explicit standby capacity fee in the quote.
>
> I'll draft a short clause that limits credits for third-party cloud-caused incidents and defines the failover measurement.
>
> — Jonas

Alex / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and the proposal packet. Procurement reviewed the matrix and a few points came back:

1) Discount: Brightline can commit to a 24-month contract if Redwood will extend 12% off hosted list pricing, or 15% off Dedicated list pricing (and include the standby capacity fee as a line item rather than an uplift). Procurement indicated they initially asked for 20% — they're willing to accept 12/15 as a compromise.

2) Insurance credits: we reviewed your sample schedule and want the crediting language in the SLA addendum and measurement windows spelled out (we'll expect automated monthly reports).

3) Escalation & on-call: we need a named engineering escalation contact or a roster with guaranteed handoffs; if Dedicated is required for 15-min remediation guarantees, we need that very clearly called out.

If you can provide an updated quote reflecting the two commercial options below, procurement will aim to circulate an internal approval next week:

- Option A (Hosted): 24-month commitment, 12% off hosted list, Rapid-Fallback SLA addendum, monthly retainer for tabletop exercises optional.
- Option B (Dedicated): 24-month commitment, 15% off Dedicated list, standby capacity fee rolled into TCV, named escalation roster, enhanced 99.995% SLA.

Please send DocuSign-ready attachments (we prefer a single quote + redlineable SLA addendum). Also include the procurement contact for contract routing: procurement@brightline.health.

If we lock this, expected go-live target for pilot is end of Q1 2027.

Regards,

Samantha Cho
